about: What changed in Pyr, for players. Newest first. Every deploy that changes something a player can see or do adds an entry at the top: 'at' is when it went live (UTC), the title names it, and each item is one plain sentence a player would understand, with no code words. The game shows these in the 'New version ready' notice. See CHANGELOG-RULE in README.md.

entries.title: Slim view: claim your next cell from the bar
items: The Cell Library's slim view arrow now always shrinks the library. With no cell to show yet, the slim bar offers Claim a new cell, which claims the next cell on the Available tab and takes you to it.
Finish your last claimed cell in slim view and the bar offers a new one, instead of opening the whole library.

entries.title: Your turn for the Proofreading Test, one click away
items: The notification that it is your turn for the Proofreading Test now opens the test when you click it.

entries.title: 3D Hover: Spotlight, Hologram and Metallic
items: Settings, 3D Hover has a new look, Spotlight: the cell under your mouse turns a little richer and the other cells in 3D dim, so it stands out gently.

Wireframe is now Hologram: the cell turns dark and glows from its edges in its own colour, with faint lines across it. It is as quick as the other looks. There is also Metallic, a dark, shiny cell with bright edges.

entries.title: Pictures in replies to your reports
items: When the team answers a report you sent, the answer can now come with a picture, like a screenshot of what they mean. Click it to see it full size.

entries.title: New players meet the top bar one tool at a time
items: A brand new player starts with only the bell in the top bar. Each tool arrives with the tutorial step that teaches it, and Nurro introduces the others.
Finishing Get Started brings the Leaderboard, Undelete and Chat, and the Merge tutorial starts by itself.
The Merge and Cut tutorials bring their tools, and finishing both brings the Cell Library.
Advanced Interface brings Find Path, Tags, Highlight and Lantern, and finishing it brings the Layer side panel.
Coming back on a second and third day fills in anything missed, and Your Week in Science arrives after a week.
Every tool is still in Profile, Settings, Toolbar Icons and in the Ctrl+K command bar, which now also opens Find Path, Highlight, Lantern, Undelete, Chat and more.
Players who already have an account keep their top bar exactly as it is.

entries.title: Settings use the whole screen
items: Profile Settings now use the full width of the profile.
Click a box's title in Settings to fold it away. Pyr remembers which ones you folded.

entries.title: Was your help request answered?
items: A day after someone replies to your help request, the bell asks whether it was answered, with a link that marks it solved right there.
Mark it solved before then and the question never comes. You only get it once per request.

entries.title: Advanced Interface: naming your layer
items: The step that asks you to name your new annotation layer now opens that layer's side panel, even when the layer was already selected.

entries.title: A tidier Layers list
items: The Layers list in the side panel matches the rest of Pyr: rounded rows, small numbers, and the layer you have selected marked in blue.

entries.title: A Help tab you can read
items: Help requests, replies and their buttons use larger text, and screenshots show at twice the size.
A long note says Show more, and opens in place.
Mark solved, which used to say Resolve, shows only for the player who asked and for admins, so nobody closes a request by mistake.

entries.title: A line for the Proofreading Test
items: When someone else is taking the Proofreading Test, its first box has Join the line. A card at the top left shows your place and a rough wait.
When the cell frees up, the first in line gets a notification, and the card says it is your turn: the cell is held for you for 10 minutes.
While anyone is waiting, the player on the cell keeps it through 15 quiet minutes instead of an hour.

entries.title: Proofreading Test: a way out
items: The bar at the top left of the Proofreading Test has Leave, to hand the cell back without a score, and its help card uses the same lettering as the rest of Pyr.

entries.title: Proofreading Test: not open yet
items: The Proofreading Test in the menu now says DO NOT TAKE. It is still being built and tried by the team; we will say when it is ready for you.

entries.title: Funnier Achievements, and the Ultramicrotome
items: Every Cell Completion and Editor Achievement now has its own line in your Trophy Case, most of them jokes, written by Celia and the Pyr team.

The Cell Completion Achievement for 2,000 cells is now the Ultramicrotome, the machine that slices brain tissue thin enough to image every cell. If you already have it, you keep it, with its new picture.

entries.title: Tidier corners
items: The music button sits in the bottom right corner of the 3D view, with the Sections box beside it, and no longer floats up when a message bar shows along the bottom.
Hovering the x, y and z letters in a view's corner opens a tidy card for the view's scale, with tips on what Default and Zoom-relative do.

entries.title: The 3D view no longer zooms out of sight
items: Scrolling in the 3D view can no longer zoom out so far that your cells disappear. Some mice in Firefox sent such big scroll steps that a few notches left the 3D view empty.
A view saved zoomed out that far now opens at the dataset's normal 3D distance.

entries.title: 3D Hover: None, and a gentler Saturate
items: Settings, 3D Hover now has None, for no highlight on the cell under your mouse. Pressing P still makes a cell pulse.
Saturate is gentler, so the cell keeps its shading.

entries.title: A pumpkin patch in the Sandbox
items: For Halloween, three cells in the Sandbox wear jack o' lanterns over their cell bodies in the 3D view, and their branches grow out through the faces. They stay until 1 November.

The pumpkin button beside the emoji button in chat has news of a rare cell type, and takes you to see it. On a pumpkin cell, the same button takes the pumpkins off and puts them back. You can also turn them off in Settings.

entries.title: Photo mode
items: Photo mode hides everything but the 3D view, fills the window with it and turns your cells slowly, like a turntable. Open it from Just for fun in the menu, from the row of buttons that appears after Share, or from the command palette.

Its small bar picks the spin speed and a black, night, grey or white background, saves a clean picture, and records one full turn as a short video you can share. Esc leaves and puts your view back as it was.
Pick centre chooses what the spin turns around: click a spot on a cell, or type a point as x, y, z.

entries.title: 3D Hover: Halo, Pulse, Wireframe and Saturate
items: New 3D Hover looks for the cell under your mouse, in Settings under 3D Hover: Halo, a slim glowing line around the cell; Pulse, a ring of light running out along the cell from your mouse when you point at it, in a colour you choose; Wireframe, the cell's 3D mesh drawn in glowing lines, finer as you zoom in; and Saturate, the cell's colour turning richer and lit from within instead of paler.
Press P with your mouse over a cell in 3D to send a ring of light along it, whichever look you use. The pulse colour can be any colour you like.
New players start with Halo. If you were already playing, the original look stays until you pick another.
With the new looks, the cell under your mouse in 2D keeps its own colour and turns more solid instead of fading to white.
Keep my display settings now also keeps Highlight on hover the way you set it when you jump to another cell.

entries.title: A roomier slim Cell Library
items: The slim Cell Library bar is wider, so your cell's whole ID shows, and it keeps the Cell Library's neuron.
The arrow that shrinks and opens the Cell Library is on the left in both views, and the next cell arrow is on the right.
Shrinking and opening the Cell Library and the Highlight box is one light bar that zips up and down, with rounded corners.
The Cell Library's settings and close buttons are bigger.

entries.title: A shorter Submit an issue
items: Submit an issue now asks for just one line: in a few words, what is it.
Want to say more? Click Add details.

entries.title: Cut points as small as merge points
items: Cut mode's Points sizes are now Small, Medium and Large, and Small is the same size as a merge point, for the tiniest pieces. The cut points no longer grow with your annotation size.

entries.title: Tidier Segments panel and Cell Library rows
items: Cells in a folder keep their jump arrow beside the ID instead of dropping to a second line.
The remove button on Pasted is no longer pushed off the edge of the panel.
The cell type list in the Complete form opens dark, like the rest of the panel.
Cell Library rows: the AI's type stays on one line, and the green bar alone marks the cell you are viewing.

entries.title: A cleaner tutorial pointer
items: Tutorial boxes now point with a thin line and a lit dot on what they mean.

entries.title: A title on every report
items: Submit an issue now asks for a short title, so the team sees at a glance what your report is about.
The Data problem choice is gone. Pick Bug, Idea or Other.

entries.title: Folders you can size, and a longer notifications window
items: Drag the grip under a folder in the Segments panel to make it taller or shorter. Double click the grip to give it its usual size.
+ Folder beside Move down puts your pasted cells straight into a new folder.
The Segments panel's green is now sky blue.
Drag the bottom edge of the notifications window to make it longer, and press Show more to see older notifications.

entries.title: What the AI predicts for each cell
items: On the Retina, each cell in the Cell Library shows the bipolar type the lab's AI predicts for it, for example 6 bipolar (t6), and so does the Cell Profile.
When you complete a cell the AI's type stands. If you are sure it is wrong, press Wrong? Correct it and choose the right one.

entries.title: Pasted coordinates find their cell
items: Coordinates pasted into the Segments box now find the cell there right away, without opening the 2D view.
Find Path failure messages go away by themselves.
Advanced Interface: clearer steps for hiding a layer, rows, Lantern and Find Path, and a shorter final mission.

entries.title: Several Pyr tabs at once
items: With Pyr open in more than one tab, each tab now keeps track of its own claimed cell, so moving to another cell in one tab no longer saves that tab's view into the cell you are working on in the other.
A setting you change in one tab now reaches your other open tabs too, instead of being put back by them.
If your graphics card runs short and the views stop drawing, which can happen with several tabs open, a notice offers to reload that tab.

entries.title: Smaller cut points
items: Cut mode has a Points choice beside Keep open: Small, Medium, Regular or Large. It sizes only the red and blue cut points, so your annotation layers keep their own size.

entries.title: The Sandbox opens with its cells
items: Opening Pyr at its plain address shows the Sandbox's starting cells again, as switching to the Sandbox does.

entries.title: Progress toward your next badge
items: The progress bars toward your next edits and cells badges now start from the last badge your count has passed, so they no longer show a negative percentage.

entries.title: Type a cell as you complete it
items: The Cell Library's Complete form now has an optional Cell type: pick from the list or type your own, and it is saved together with the completion, so there is no separate step in the Cell Profile.

entries.title: Boxes, circles, arrows and text on screenshots
items: When you mark up a screenshot you can now draw a box, a circle or an arrow, and add text you can drag into place, as well as using the pen.
Hold Shift to draw a perfect square or circle.

entries.title: The 2D view no longer freezes
items: After switching between 2D only and 2D + 3D, or after moving on to your next cell, the 2D view sometimes stopped loading new slices until you pressed Space twice or reloaded. It now keeps loading.

entries.title: Your profile fits a smaller screen
items: On a laptop screen, or with the browser zoomed in, your profile now fits the window, with its close button in the corner where you can reach it.

entries.title: New full screen and split screen buttons
items: With a mouse, the corner buttons of the 2D and 3D views are now icons in the style of the rest of Pyr, and each spells out what it does when you point at it: 3D only, 2D only, or 2D + 3D to come back to split screen.

entries.title: Your profile opens without a jump
items: Your profile builds from the top down: each row appears whole, with its line, numbers and curve, once its numbers are in, instead of pieces landing as they arrive. Nothing shifts.
The light that ran around the edge of the profile is gone, now that the profile fills the window.
The browser tab now says Pyr, not neuroglancer.
In the Trophy Case the tiles show each Achievement's name and threshold; its description shows when you pick it.

entries.title: Numbered annotations, in folders
items: Every annotation in a layer's list now has a number, in the list's order.
+ Folder makes a folder for your annotations. Name it, fold it, put one folder inside another, or delete it.
Drag an annotation's row to move it up or down the list, or onto a folder to put it in.
Ctrl+click or Shift+click picks several annotations to move to a folder or delete together.
Pick a color on a folder's dot to draw its annotations in that color. Untick Color its annotations to give them the layer's color again.
Your order and folders are saved with the layer, so saved views and shared links keep them.

entries.title: A way back from 3D only
items: After you switch to 3D only, a 2D + 3D button in the corner of the 3D view brings the 2D image back. Space still does the same.

entries.title: Proofreading Test results, biggest misses first
items: The Proofreading Test, still a work in progress, now lists your biggest misses first and pins at most 25 of them on the cell, so a long list stays readable.

entries.title: What a connectome is, in Get Started
items: Page 2 of the Get Started tutorial now says what a connectome is, with a link to Connectome 101.

entries.title: Tidier Segments panel on tablets
items: On a tablet the Segments panel buttons no longer pile up on top of the first cell after a split, a merge or a tap.
Each cell's remove button is now at the far right of its row, right under the heading's remove all.
In the report form, the box for console messages is greyed out when there are none to send.

entries.title: Pasted coordinates show their cell
items: Coordinates pasted into the Segments box stay there while the cell is found, and the new row shows where it came from.
Tutorial boxes point with a tab from their own edge and open in place.
Advanced Interface asks you to try a step before skipping it, and adds a second Highlight color.

entries.title: The Sandbox opens close in
items: The Sandbox's 2D view now opens close enough in for its cells to load.
In Advanced Interface, the arrow settles after two sweeps, Checked highlights show pink, and the memo opens the Segments tab.

entries.title: A new Advanced Interface tutorial
items: Advanced Interface is rebuilt in four short parts: marking what you see, working with cells, finding your way, and putting it together to find where a merger starts.
The tutorials now run Get Started, Merge, Cut, Advanced Interface, then the Merger Sandbox.
Tutorial boxes sit right next to what they point at, with a new arrow, copy buttons for coordinates and IDs, and hints you can hover.
Many steps move on by themselves when you do the thing they ask.
New annotation layers start with golden Pyr gems.
The Render tab is split into Colors, 2D view, 3D view and More, each with its own Opacity.
Pasting coordinates into the Segments box opens the 2D view close in, so the cell there is found.
Opening Highlight closes Find Path, and Submit stops pulsing once a path is found.
The menu closes when you click outside it.
In the Sandbox, 2D EM and 3D segmentation can no longer be removed by accident.
Chat no longer opens below the screen after a reload, and the Quest ID check shows the full ID.

entries.title: An easier to spot search box in Segments
items: The box at the top of the Segments panel, where you paste cell IDs or coordinates or search by name, now looks like a box to type in, with more room around it.

entries.title: A cleaner annotation layer panel
items: An annotation layer's panel now shows its name at the top like a file name. Click the pencil (or the name) to rename it.
The tools start right under the name, and the delete button turns red when you point at it.
Settings for filtering annotations by linked cells are under Advanced at the bottom of the panel.

entries.title: Cut mode keeps your cells on screen
items: Pressing C no longer hides the cells you are working on to show some old cell. Cut points left on a cell you are not showing, from an earlier visit or a saved view, are cleared as cut mode opens, and the cut bar offers Undo for a few seconds.
A cell with cut points on it can now be hidden or removed while cut mode is closed. Before, it kept coming back.
Ask for Edit Access: a cut example saves only while the cell its points are on is shown, so the reviewer sees the cell with the points.

entries.title: Quests load all day
items: The quest list no longer stops loading partway through the day with a Too Many Requests error. It had a daily limit that was far too low for busy questers.

entries.title: A tidier Learn more menu
items: The old Proofreading Guide link is gone from the menu and the command search, because it no longer matched Pyr. The tutorials in the menu cover everything it did.

entries.title: Tablets: back to 2D with 3D, and a tidy Segments heading
items: On a tablet, choosing 3D only now leaves a 2D + 3D button to go back, and split screen has 2D only and 3D only buttons.
On a touch screen the In view heading in the Segments panel no longer stacks Select on top of the count, so Select works with one tap.

entries.title: Ask for Edit Access, right in Pyr
items: You can now ask for edit access to the retina inside the game: open the menu and choose Ask for Edit Access, at the very bottom.
Place cut or merge points on ten mistakes you find, without submitting the edits, and save each view with one click. Pyr keeps every point and your notes.
Send all ten for review. The team looks at every point and answers in your notifications, with notes on each example.
Change any example before or after you send, as often as you like. You are never locked out.
Press Slim to make the box small on a laptop screen.

entries.title: Open a cell from chat in a new tab
items: A cell ID in chat is now a link: right click it and open it in a new tab, or middle click or Ctrl click it, to look at the cell without leaving what you are doing. A plain click still jumps to it here.
If you minimize the chat, it stays minimized after you reload Pyr.

entries.title: Claimed cells stay the cell you claimed
items: After you edit a cell you claimed, completing it no longer says the cell is not in the sheet, and the claim no longer turns into a neighbouring cell.
Claims already affected are put back to their own cell the next time you open the Cell Library.

entries.title: Tidier Segments headings, and a safer folder delete
items: Every heading in the Segments panel reads the same way: the eye on the left, in line with the cells' eyes, then the name and count, and a folder's color dot on the right above the cells' status marks.
Hover a heading for its buttons. The ones that remove things sit last on the right, set apart by a thin line, and the trash can is red so it never looks like copy.
A folder's ✕ asks what to do: keep its cells in view, remove only the hidden ones, or remove them all with the folder. Enter keeps them.
A long cell ID ends in … on hover so the buttons never sit on top of it, and each folder's colored line now starts at its heading.

entries.title: No more grey flashes when scrolling through slices
items: When you scroll through slices in the 2D view, the picture no longer goes grey for a moment every 16 slices. It now shows a blurry version straight away and sharpens as it loads.

entries.title: Completion messages in front of the Cell Library
items: The card after you submit a quest cell, and the messages after you complete a cell, now show in front of the Cell Library instead of behind it.

entries.title: Calm screen
items: A new setting, Calm screen: no animations or glows. It is in Settings, under User Interface. It stops the animations, takes away the glows and the twinkling dots, and makes your profile plainer. Your cells and the 3D view stay as they are.
A special award you receive now shows on your profile the next time you open it, without reloading Pyr.

entries.title: Quest layers stay with their quests
items: Looking at any cell from the Cell Library, or opening one of your claimed cells, now puts the quest's annotation layers away first, even in a new tab. They no longer show up on other cells or get saved into a claimed cell's view.

entries.title: Profile curves: none on small screens, a settled draw on large ones
items: On a laptop or a small screen zoomed in, your profile shows the numbers without the curves. The curves stay on larger screens.
On larger screens each curve now draws once after the frame has settled, instead of snapping to its end a moment in.

entries.title: Lists in team replies
items: Replies from the team about your reports now show their numbered and bulleted lists as lists.

entries.title: Easier on phones and tablets
items: Swiping one finger through the 2D images moves through the slices more slowly, so you can stop where you want.
Hold one finger still on a spot to move the view there. It now takes just over half a second.
On a touch screen the Segments panel has a Select button: tap cells to pick them, then move them to a folder, show, hide, color or remove them together.
On a phone the corner button switches between 3D only and 2D with 3D.

entries.title: Quest work stays with its quest cell
items: Jumping from a quest cell to one of your claimed cells now saves your quest work first and takes the quest's layers out of the view. Before, they came along, and your quest cell could reopen showing the wrong cell.

entries.title: Restore all settings to default
items: Settings has a new button at the bottom, Restore all settings to default. It asks first, then puts every setting back to how Pyr starts, on all your computers. Your flag, bio, cells and progress stay as they are.

entries.title: A new Segments panel, with folders
items: The Seg. tab is now called Segments, rebuilt to make your cells easier to manage.
Paste cell IDs into the box to add them straight to your view, under Pasted. Paste coordinates to go there and add the cell at that spot.
Make folders to group your cells: drag cells onto a folder, fold it away, put folders inside folders, and drag folders to reorder them.
Click a folder's color dot to give every cell in it one color. A checkbox lets cells you add later take that color too.
Ctrl+click (Cmd+click on a Mac) or Shift+click to pick several cells, then move, show, hide, color or remove them together from the bar at the bottom.
Click a cell's ID to open its menu. The trash can on a row removes that cell from your view; the one on a heading removes them all after asking, and Shift+click removes only the hidden ones.
Type a name like Pyramidal to find your cells by type.
The bounding box controls and the Select tool are in the Render tab, and the cell layer's panel shows its name and a close button only.

entries.title: A new Müller cell in Meet the cells
items: Retina's Meet the cells tour now shows a single Müller glia cell. The one before was two cells stuck together.
In the Cilia Quest, the explanation for No cilium (BB & DC clear) is clearer: the centrioles are visible and clearly differentiated, with the basal body closer to the surface.

entries.title: Choose how sharp the 2D images are
items: A new setting, 2D image detail, lets you draw the 2D images at Half or Quarter detail so they load much faster on a slow connection. It is in Settings, under User Interface. Full stays the default, and your choice is kept on your account.

entries.title: Your viewer settings stay put
items: Prefetching, concurrent chunk requests and the memory limits you set in Viewer settings are now kept on your account. Opening a quest cell, a link or reloading no longer puts them back to the defaults.

entries.title: Lighter on the server
items: The leaderboard refreshes every two minutes instead of every minute, and asks for far less each time. Opening a player's card loads their all-time totals.
The bell checks for new notifications once a minute and asks only for what is new. A new notification still appears within a minute.

entries.title: Tap to place on phones and tablets
items: On a touch screen, one tap now places a point in Cut, Merge and Find Path, the same as Ctrl+click. Two quick taps still show or hide a cell.
One tap also places annotation points, and Highlight points while the Highlight box is open.
On a touch screen the Cut and Merge bar says tap and shows buttons in place of keys.

entries.title: Tablets keep the top bar during Cut and Merge
items: On a tablet, starting Cut or Merge from the top bar no longer slides the whole page up and hides the top bar.

entries.title: Cell Profile on the right, steadier chat scrolling
items: The Cell Profile opens along the right edge of the page instead of over the cells you are looking at. Close it with its X or by clicking outside it.
Scrolling to the top of the chat loads one page of older messages at a time, so a quick swipe no longer races far back. Scroll up again to see more.

entries.title: Cell Profile and reply screenshots
items: The Cell Profile opens over the side panel and has its own X to close it. Clicking outside it still closes it too.
A screenshot you add to a reply now stays attached. Clicking in the screenshot window used to close the reply and lose the picture.

entries.title: Your Cilia Quest work is kept
items: The quest you are working on is marked Active in the Quests tab, and each of your quests shows its cell ID.

Your annotations on a quest are saved as you place them. Open on the quest you are on goes to the cell without reloading it, and opening one of your quests again brings your saved work back. Save now saves it at once.

entries.title: See the segment ID under a cell's label
items: A new setting, Show the segment ID under a cell's label, writes each typed cell's segment ID under its label in the segment list. It is in Settings, under User Interface, and is off unless you turn it on.

entries.title: Your work is kept when CAVE is down
items: When CAVE is not answering, marking a cell proofread or saving a cell type no longer asks you to try again. Pyr keeps it, counts it right away, and sends it to CAVE as soon as CAVE is back, under your name.
You will see a message when something is waiting, and another when it has been sent. Unmarking a cell before then simply takes it off the list.
Replying to the team now ends on the lit up neuron alone.

entries.title: Jumps take you straight to the cell
items: Jumping to a cell on another dataset, from chat, the Cell Library or My cells, now shows just that cell, without the dataset's starter cells, and no longer reloads the page on the way.

entries.title: Easier 3D controls
items: In the 3D view, scroll now zooms in and out, and dragging with the right mouse button slides the view. A right click without dragging still centres the view where you clicked.
Ctrl+scroll and Shift+drag keep working too, so use whichever you like. The 2D views are unchanged: scroll still moves through the sections.
Retina opens on two current cells, in blue and gold.
You can wave in chat: 👋 is now in the emoji choices.
The music button sits beside the 3D view's Sections box instead of above it, and the green segment colour is a softer green.
Your profile shows your latest 10 completed cells, with the rest a click away in My cells, and cells finished from the Cell Library show their segment ID.

entries.title: Your profile lists only your own completed cells
items: Recently completed cells on a profile now lists the cells that player completed. Before, it could show cells completed by someone else who had used the same browser.

entries.title: Music on, and replies that show they arrived
items: Pyr Radio now plays when you start, unless you have turned it off. If you turn it off, it stays off.
The music button sits on the same line as the coordinates, and moves up only when something is under it.
Replying to the team shows each step while it sends, then lets you know the team has it.

entries.title: The Proofreading Test gets a clock
items: The Proofreading Test, still a work in progress, has a 60 minute time limit. The time left shows at the top left, and when it runs out your cell is scored as it stands.

entries.title: Tutorials menu numbers line up
items: The numbers in the Tutorials menu now line up in one column on the left.
The Proofreading Test, still a work in progress, shows a loading card while it gets your cell and while it scores, and gives you an End layer with Pyr gems for marking branch ends.

entries.title: The Proofreading Test is marked WIP
items: The Proofreading Test in the Tutorials menu now says WIP, for work in progress. It is still being tried out, so please leave it for now.

entries.title: Cut tutorial: two points on each side
items: The first cut in the Cut tutorial now asks for 2 red and 2 blue points. With one point a side the cut took only half the axon off.
If a cut there leaves half the axon attached, the box says so and shows where the rest goes.
Pressing C or M a second time now says the tool is off, and how to turn it back on.
Small wording changes from tester feedback.

entries.title: Cut tutorial: half a cut is not the whole job
items: In the 2D cut of the Cut tutorial, cutting the axon off only partway no longer counts. The box says half is done and shows where the rest of the cut goes.
Practice views no longer show every hint point twice.

entries.title: Merge tutorial: the second merge shows where to click
items: The second merge in the Merge tutorial now shows pink gems on the two spots to click, as the first one does.

entries.title: Chat keeps working when live updates are down
items: If the live connection behind chat goes down, you can still read and send messages. New ones arrive every few seconds, and the dot at the top of chat turns amber until the live connection is back.

entries.title: The Cilia Quest
items: The Cell Library has a Quests tab. On Retina, claim a starburst cell, mark its basal body, daughter centriole and cilium centerline in the layers that open with it, and press Submit. The cell does not need to be proofread. You can hold three cells at a time.

Your answer, your notes and a share link of your view go to the lab's sheet with your name and the date. Submitting brings a celebration and your count, and your profile shows how many quests you have completed.

Annotation layers have a new tool, the polyline: hold Ctrl and click along a line, press Enter to finish, Backspace to take a point back, Esc to cancel. It is the same polyline the lab's own viewer draws.

The quest's Instructions link the lab's guide, its training video and a reference: three real example cells, annotated by the lab, each saying which status it shows and when to use it. In any annotation list, a description now shows in full where it used to be cut at one line.

entries.title: Reply to the team with a screenshot
items: When the team asks you for a reply about a report, you can now add a screenshot, your current view and your recent console messages, the same as on a report.
The screenshot shows the game, not the message you are answering.

entries.title: Preview a cut before you make it
items: In cut mode, place your red and blue points and press Preview. The cell is coloured in 3D to show what would stay with the red points and what would go with the blue ones, so you can see where the cut will fall before you make it.
Around your points the colours follow the supervoxels themselves, so the edge of the cut is exact there. Farther along the cell they show which side each branch ends up on.
Nothing is cut until you press Submit cut. The colours go away when you move a point, submit, or leave cut mode.

entries.title: Reply to the team about your report
items: When the team asks you a question about a report you sent, the notification now has a box where you can write back.

entries.title: Pyr gems stay on your annotation layers
items: When you set an annotation layer to show its points as Pyr gems, the layer of the same name on the next cell you open shows gems too. Before, it went back to dots with every new cell.

entries.title: Steadier segment list, and help requests read better in chat
items: Removing a segment no longer flashes a bar along the bottom, so the legend under the list stays still.
After you click the legend, pressing Enter to send a merge or a cut no longer starts a legend check.
The cell menu shows how many claims you really have left, counting cells claimed in the Cell Library.
A help request shows in chat as New help request from the player, without the SOS emoji.

entries.title: The profile keeps its shape on a very wide screen
items: On a very wide screen the profile overview no longer stretches across the whole window: it keeps the proportions it has on a normal screen and sits in the middle of the frame.
In each row of your profile, the count of what is left to your next Achievement now sits above the arrow to the Trophy Case, where the row ends, instead of at the far edge of the window.

entries.title: Retina: a claimed cell shows WIP in the sheet
items: When you claim a Retina cell, its Status in the sheet is set to WIP, so you can see in the sheet which cells are yours to do.
Completing the cell replaces WIP with the status you choose. Releasing it clears WIP along with your name.

entries.title: New annotation layers open at your point size
items: A new annotation layer you make now opens at the size you last set on the Size slider, and the Annotate point button keeps that size.

entries.title: Your annotation point size is remembered
items: Set the Size slider on an annotation layer once, and new annotation layers and new workspaces open at that size. A layer keeps its own size if you set one for it.

entries.title: Shift+L opens and closes the Cell Library
items: Press Shift+L to open and close the Cell Library. The shortcut is now shown when you hover its icon in the top bar and its close button.

entries.title: Cells the lab finished are not offered again
items: On Retina, a cell the lab's own sheet marks as complete no longer offers Mark as Proofread or Claim in its Delta menu. The menu says the lab has already proofread it.
A cell you completed in Pyr keeps its Unmark, and a cell you already hold keeps its Release.

entries.title: Dots for your Merger Sandbox progress
items: Your progress in the Merger Sandbox is shown as plain dots in the full box too.

entries.title: Skip sits beside Help me
items: In the Merger Sandbox, Skip is now a button to the left of Help me.

entries.title: Skip, when there is nothing to skip to
items: Skipping your last unsolved merger used to show it as still fused. Skip this one now only appears when there is another merger to go to.

entries.title: Merger Sandbox: Next is the main button again
items: The main button in the Merger Sandbox is Next, which checks your cut. Skip this one is a small link in the full box.
The slim bar opens a line of text when there is news, such as a cut that went through but did not finish the job.
The slim bar shows your progress as plain dots.

entries.title: Notices at the bottom no longer cover the legend
items: When a notice or tool bar runs along the bottom of the screen, the segment list legend and the Sections switch in the 3D view move up so you can still see and use them.

entries.title: The slim Merger Sandbox box is one bar
items: Folded, the Merger Sandbox box is now a single bar: your progress and Skip. Open it again with the small arrow for the hint and Help me.

entries.title: Retina cells show what the lab knows
items: On Retina, a cell the lab's own sheet lists now shows it in the segment list: its mark says proofread, typed or done, and its class and type stand in for its ID.
The Delta menu fills in the same way. Completion Status and Cell Type say what the lab's sheet says wherever nothing is saved in Pyr yet, and the menu's title is the cell's class and type.
What you save in Pyr always wins, and the lab's sheet does not change your stats.

entries.title: Cut mode can stay open after a cut
items: Tick Keep open after a cut, at the right end of the cut bar, and cut mode stays on after each cut, ready for the next one. Esc or C closes it. It is off unless you turn it on, and your choice is remembered.
A cut the server refuses no longer leaves the bar waiting: the spinner stops and you can try again.

entries.title: The lab's notes in the Delta menu
items: On Retina, the Delta menu of a cell now shows what the lab's own retina sheet says about it: its status, cell class and type. It is there to read, and it does not change your stats.

entries.title: Your profile: a range for the curves, and cells identified
items: Choose the range of the two curves on your profile: all time, 90, 30 or 7 days. At 7 days a curve ends on the Past 7d number under it. The choice is remembered.
Beside your name, a count of the cells you identified: cells whose type you set in Pyr, each once. Unknown or Unsure does not count, and neither does the Sandbox.
Today, Past 7d and All time now sit on one line, with the merge and split counts under them on one line too.
The Cells completed and Edits blocks take more of their row, so a long count never runs under your Achievements.
On a laptop screen the merge and split counts stack in two short lines when the row is short of room.

entries.title: A slim Merger Sandbox box
items: The Merger Sandbox box can be folded down to a slim strip: your progress, the hint, Help me and Skip. Press the small arrow at the end of the row of gems. It remembers your choice.

entries.title: More datasets say where they came from
items: MICrONS, H01, MANC, MAOL, CA3 and the Pinky Sandbox now show their source on their cards.

entries.title: Batch Processor: each cell is typed at its own point
items: When you set a cell type for a group, each cell is now saved at the point you saved inside it, so the type lands on the right cell.
A cell with no saved point is skipped and counted. Put the crosshairs inside it, press Save point, then apply again.

entries.title: Hemibrain joins the datasets
items: Hemibrain is here to explore: about half of a fruit fly's central brain, from Janelia. Turn it on in your profile's Datasets tab or in Settings.
Dataset cards now say where each dataset came from.

entries.title: Merger Sandbox: a good cut counts, and no more going round in circles
items: Two mergers were refusing cuts that were right. They now accept a cut made at the join even when the points sit a little to one side.
If the merger you have left is being put back to its starting state, the box waits and opens it for you, instead of handing you one you have already solved.

entries.title: Skip a merger, and less confetti
items: The Merger Sandbox has a Skip button, to move on to another merger and come back later.
One merger was taken out for now, so there are 7.
Confetti is thrown only when a cut is confirmed, not when you press Try again.
The result boxes are smaller, with a new Nurro for a merger that is still fused.

entries.title: No more flashing panels in the Merger Sandbox
items: Each merger now opens straight in 3D. The 2D images and the side panel no longer flash open and shut as it loads.

entries.title: A cell type that did not save now says so
items: If the server does not save a cell type, the menu now shows an error and asks you to try again. Before, it could say Saved when the type had not been saved.
The Batch Processor counts a cell type the server refused as failed.

entries.title: The profile fills the window
items: Your profile now fills the whole window, with more room for everything in it.
Your profile counts your work in Pyr on all of its datasets, not only the dataset on screen. Only work done in Pyr counts.

Cells completed shows today, the past 7 days and all time, the same three windows as edits, and above each a small curve draws your running total from your first day to today. Point at it to read any day.

Each of cells, edits and days is one row: the latest Achievement you earned, your numbers and curve, and the rest of that track's Achievements beside them. A circuit line runs across the top of each row, breaks at two pads, and from the second one fills toward your next Achievement, with how many to go at its end. Your all time number stands out in its own type. Achievement names show when you point at them.
Days helping science in Pyr shows your latest Days Achievement beside your total. Your streak stays on the right.
Your recently completed cells are listed even on a new device.
If you have a username, your profile is titled with it.
Cells, edits and days each have their own colour on the profile, the same as their Achievement sections: sky blue, gold and purple. The Last 14 Days chart uses the same two.
Your Special Awards sit beside your name. The profile fits the window without scrolling; your recently completed cells scroll in their own box.

entries.title: More reactions in chat
items: The reaction picker in chat has a + at the end. It opens 38 more reactions, including 👌 and 👏.
Chat messages now start at the left edge of the chat, so there is more room for the words.

entries.title: Chat: a little more room beside your own messages
items: The bar that marks your own messages in chat no longer sits right against the words.

entries.title: A warning before Ctrl+W closes Pyr
items: If you press Ctrl+W by mistake, for example reaching for Ctrl+2 or Ctrl+3, your browser now asks before it closes the tab. Refreshing the page does not ask.

entries.title: Choose what you see when you complete a cell
items: In Settings, When I complete a cell, show lets you keep the full congratulations, switch to a small note at the top of the screen, or show nothing.
The pills for top bar icons in Settings show short names and no longer run out of their panel. Hover a pill for the full description.

entries.title: Achievements always reach chat
items: An Achievement you earn is now always announced in chat. Sometimes the line was missed when the count was confirmed a moment late.

entries.title: The segment list keeps its place
items: Removing a segment from a long list no longer makes the list jump up. It stays where you were.

entries.title: Cell types and completions stay with the cell after an edit
items: A cell type or completion you save in the Δ menu now stays on the cell after you merge or cut it, even though the cell gets a new ID.
To save a cell type, the crosshairs must be inside the cell, the same as for Mark as Proofread. If they are not, the menu tells you where they are.

entries.title: Announcements in chat show their picture
items: An announcement in chat, such as a new blog post, now shows a small version of its picture beside the text.

entries.title: A Proofreading Test, on trial
items: A Proofreading Test is coming to the Tutorials menu: one Sandbox cell with several mistakes on it, and the server checks your work and tells you what you found and what you missed.
It is being tried out by Ames first. When it appears in your menu, please leave it to her for a few days; passing it grants nothing yet.

entries.title: Nurro knows the Merger Sandbox
items: Nurro, the guide, now knows that a merger is fixed with a cut, and how the Merger Sandbox works.
The extra help in the tutorials has an x to close it.
The Merger Sandbox box has a plainer title, and its hint now reads: Ctrl+click to add points, and remember to press G to switch the cut colour group.

entries.title: Editor Achievements come closer together
items: The Achievements you earn by editing now come at steadier steps: every 100 edits up to 500, then 750 and 1,000, every 500 up to 5,000, every 1,000 up to 10,000, every 2,000 up to 20,000, every 5,000 up to 100,000, and every 10,000 after that.
Nobody loses an Achievement. If your count already passes a new mark, it shows as earned in your Trophy Case.

entries.title: Start the Merger Sandbox again
items: Once you have solved every merger, opening the Merger Sandbox asks whether you want to start again, and counts from zero if you do. Your Achievement stays yours.
The count of mergers is smaller and quieter, and its glint of light runs once.
The last box shows its caption when you hover over the picture, and its button now says Finish.

entries.title: Pyr gems count your mergers
items: The Merger Sandbox count is now a chain of Pyr gems, one per merger, lit as you solve them.

entries.title: A new look for the Merger Sandbox count
items: Your progress in the Merger Sandbox is now a chain of small diamonds, one per merger, that light up as you solve them.
The Selection panel on the right stays closed while you are in the Merger Sandbox.

entries.title: Mergers 7 and 8 check the cut more closely
items: Mergers 7 and 8 in the Merger Sandbox now count a cut only when it is made at the join. A cut somewhere else on the cell no longer passes.

entries.title: Complete the Sandbox
items: The last box of the Merger Sandbox has a new picture and a Complete the Sandbox button.
The Achievement for cutting every merger now arrives when you press that button, not before the box.

entries.title: A smaller box in the Merger Sandbox
items: The Merger Sandbox box is shorter, with the title Can you solve all 8 merger mysteries?
The layer side panel closes when a practice cell opens, so there is more room to work.
Each merger now opens in 3D. Press Space for the 2D images.
Still need help? no longer shows before you have pressed Help me, and the empty band at the bottom of the box is gone.

entries.title: A calmer progress strip in the Merger Sandbox
items: The strip that counts your mergers is dimmer and reads like an instrument: a thin lit edge for each one cut, and a sweep of light on the one in hand.

entries.title: Cell Completion Achievements at round numbers
items: The Cell Completion Achievements now come at round numbers: 1, 5, 10, 15, 20, 30, 40, 50, 75, 100, and on from there, up to 54,000 cells.
Every Achievement you already earned is yours to keep, even where its number went up.

entries.title: A progress strip in the Merger Sandbox
items: The Merger Sandbox shows a strip with one cell per merger: lit for each one you have cut, glowing on the one in hand.
Merger 6 now notices your cut. It was checking two spots on the same neuron, so no cut could count.

entries.title: A kinder note when a cut is not the whole job
items: When your cut goes through but the two neurons are still joined, the Cut tutorial and the Merger Sandbox now say so plainly: good job, but there is more to cut.

entries.title: Tutorial help says the right click
items: The help in the Merge and Cut tutorials now says to click the 3D segmentation tab to select it, which is how it works now.
It also suggests sharing your view in chat when you ask for help.

entries.title: Share my view waits for your message
items: Share my view in chat now puts a My view chip on the message box instead of posting at once, so you can type a few words first and then send.
The x on the chip removes it.

entries.title: A new Achievement in the Merger Sandbox
items: Cut every merger in the Merger Sandbox to earn the Pyramidal Precision Achievement.
If you have already cut them all, it is yours the next time you open Pyr.

entries.title: Three more mergers in the Merger Sandbox
items: The Merger Sandbox now has 8 fused cells to cut apart, up from 5.
Help me shows where the points go on the new ones too.

entries.title: A new look for the Lantern box
items: The Lantern box now has the same circuit board look as the layer tabs, with a line of light along its top that runs down the sides.
The Lantern box slides open from the left when you light the Lantern (Shift+N).

entries.title: A builder's counter on Amy's profile
items: Amy's profile now shows how many changes have been saved to Pyr's code, and how many times a new version has gone live.

entries.title: Roomier notifications, clearer chat jumps, steadier Highlight
items: A long notification with a wide picture now gives the text the larger share of the card, so it is no longer squeezed down the right side.
Clicking a cell ID from another dataset in chat says which dataset the cell is in, and the button takes you there by name.
Where a cell loops back on itself, To soma and Beyond in Highlight follow the way that is shorter in distance along the cell.

entries.title: Lantern mode
items: Lantern mode lights the cell around the centre of your view and dims the rest, so you can check a big cell one part at a time. The light follows you as you move.
Turn it on with the lantern in the toolbar, or press Shift+N.
Set how far the light reaches and how bright it is in the small Lantern bar. Drag the bar by its grip to put it where you like.
Thank you to Krzysztof Kruk for the idea.

entries.title: Chat buttons stay out of the way
items: The reply and reaction buttons that appear when you point at a chat message now sit just above it, so they no longer cover its last words.
The pin is a simple outline now.

entries.title: Chat: new message line, pinned messages, search by day
items: A line in chat shows where the messages you have not seen begin.
Your own messages are marked with a thin bar. You can switch it off in Settings.
A message can be pinned to the top of chat for everyone. Click it to go to the message, or hide it for yourself.
Search chat by day with on:10/8, after:yesterday or before:2026-10-01.

entries.title: The last annotations in the list can be reached
items: The annotation list now scrolls all the way to its last row. Before, the end of a long list was cut off.

entries.title: Click an annotation to find it in the list
items: Click an annotation in the 2D or 3D view and it is selected in the annotation list, which scrolls to show it.
The previous and next arrows above the annotation list are larger and easier to press.

entries.title: Bigger pictures in notifications
items: When you open a notification with a wide picture, the picture is now much larger and the window uses more of your screen.

entries.title: Chat: search, bold and underline, and your own messages
items: Search chat with the magnifier at the top of the chat. Click a result to see it in the conversation, and press Esc to go back.
Type *bold* or _underline_ in a message, or select text and press Ctrl+B or Ctrl+U.
In Settings, switch on Mark my own messages in chat to put a thin bar beside what you wrote.

entries.title: Notifications stay with you
items: A notification you have already received stays in your feed, even after the team stops sending it to new people.

entries.title: Highlight: cleaner starts, calmer color
items: A mark made with To soma or Beyond now starts exactly where you clicked, and no longer runs a little way in the other direction.
The newest mark is still the brightest, without burning out to a pale blank.
The point you clicked stays in view after its mark is made, until you place the next one.

entries.title: Highlight: to the soma, and beyond a point
items: In Highlight mode, after your first Ctrl + click, To soma marks the way from that point back to the soma.
Beyond marks every branch on the far side of that point, away from the soma.
If the cell's soma is not on record, Pyr asks you to click it once, and keeps it as a point in a Soma layer.
A two click mark that the server could not trace is now drawn from the cell's own branch map instead of failing.
Shift + H turns Highlight mode on and off.
The Show and Hide switch in the Highlight box is quieter.
Thanks to Krzysztof Kruk for the idea.

entries.title: Truer edit counts and a few extras
items: Edits are now counted only when the server confirms them, so a merge or cut is never counted twice.
A merge that fails tells you why, right under it in the Merge Queue.
Drag your silver and bronze favorites into the order you like.
Chat says what kind of cell was completed, such as a retina cell.
The jump and delete buttons on each annotation are larger.

entries.title: More favorites in your Trophy Case
items: You can now pick up to ten bronze favorites, alongside your gold favorite and five silver ones.
Drag a Trophy Case section by its heading to put your sections in the order you like. Visitors see your order too.
A favorite that no longer shows does not use up one of your places.
In the Cell Library, search for one available cell and the Claim button takes that cell and the ones after it.

entries.title: A daily note of what changed
items: On any evening when Pyr changed that day, a notification lists what is new, in the same words as the version notice.
Days with no changes send nothing.

entries.title: The 2D image arrives sooner
items: In the Sandbox a view now fetches about 60 MB of image instead of 100 MB, and moving to the next slab or panning no longer waits on pieces the screen cannot show.
Scrolling and panning no longer start large downloads of slabs far ahead of you while the slab you are looking at is still arriving.
A piece of image that fails to arrive is tried again instead of staying grey until you move the view.
The first Retina pieces no longer wait for a large decoder to start.
A saved view that asked for a blurry image is shown at full detail.

entries.title: Chat celebrates Loyalty Achievements
items: When you earn a Loyalty Achievement, chat now says so, and anyone can click the line to see your Trophy Case.
If you earned yours this morning, your highest one is announced the next time you open Pyr.

entries.title: Shortcuts, counts and who is online
items: Shift+L opens and closes the Cell Library.
In Settings you can choose which tab the Cell Library opens on.
Each annotation layer shows how many annotations it holds.
Click the online count in chat to see who is there. A name opens that player's profile.
The Merge Queue opens beside the chat, and you can drag it by its header to wherever you like.

entries.title: Loyalty Achievements
items: Loyalty Achievements are here: one for each milestone of days you do science in Pyr, from your second day to a full year.
Your days add up forever and never have to be in a row, so taking a break costs you nothing.
Find them in the Trophy Case on your profile, with a count of the days to your next one.

entries.title: Tutorial Achievements and small fixes
items: Finishing a tutorial now records its Achievement for every player. If you finished one before and it is missing, it arrives the next time you sign in.
After Claim 10, My Cells opens at the top, where your new cells are.
When an award is given to a group, every player's award shows in chat.
Dataset Stats explains where its count of your cells comes from.
The spreadsheet keeps your name spelled the way it already has it.

entries.title: A new look for Cut and Merge
items: The Cut and Merge bars have a cleaner look, with the buttons together on the left.
Merge has a Clear button again, which empties the whole Merge Queue.
Each merge in the queue shows when it is submitting, done or failed.
In Cut, the G key lights up without pulsing, and switching between red and blue is calmer.

entries.title: Chat awards, calmer loading, easier merging
items: Chat now announces special awards, and you can click the line to see that player's Trophy Case.
The 2D loading card waits until the view has been still for a moment, so it stays out of the way while you trace.
Hovering a segment in the Merge Queue lights it up in the 2D and 3D views.
With merge open, Ctrl+click on an annotation layer places an annotation, so you do not have to close merge first.

entries.title: Help requests work better
items: A screenshot taken from the help form shows your view, without the Cell Library in the way.
A help request now saves the cell you are working on, not whichever one the mouse last touched.
Jumping to a request with no cell takes you to the right place and leaves your cells alone.
Ask for Help in the Delta menu lets you choose which annotation layers to point the helper at.

entries.title: New version notice
items: Pyr tells you when it has been updated while you were playing, so you can reload and get the newest fixes.

entries.title: Mentor mode and Team mode (first version)
items: Mentor mode: press Join on a help request to offer to step into that player's view. They choose whether to accept.
Team mode: press Team up on this cell in the Help tab and invite players by name to work on one cell together.
In a session you share the cell, your marks, and where each of you is looking. Jump takes you to a teammate, Follow keeps you with them.
When one teammate marks the cell complete, everyone on the team is credited.

entries.title: Clearer messages
items: If you paste a cell ID with digits missing from the start, Pyr tells you instead of showing an empty view.
Another player's profile no longer shows your own numbers for a moment while it loads.

entries.title: Your stats, counted right
items: Your cells in Dataset Stats are matched to your name whether or not it is typed with capitals.
Cells you proofread outside Pyr on other datasets show on your profile's Datasets tab. They do not count toward Achievements.

entries.title: Help requests keep your marks
items: A help request now saves your whole view, so a helper who opens it sees your annotations and highlights.
The link to your view fills itself in. You do not need to click anything.
You can point a helper at any of your annotation layers, or all of them.
Switch here and jumping to a request on another dataset now bring you back to the Help tab and finish the jump.

entries.title: Smoother lists and highlights
items: With many cells open, you can scroll all the way to the bottom of the cell list.
The Highlight box has one Show or Hide switch for all your highlights, in 2D and 3D.
